subject: Heterogeneous commit + price-hold proposal for Atlas Health renewal
messages:
From: Maya Singh <m.singh@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: John Rivera <john.rivera@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation kickoff — capacity growth ask

Karthik —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick summary from our side: Atlas expects a 2.5x token increase across our chat/summary workloads next year; procurement wants a firm renewal number, and legal will want price protection for Q1 while we ramp. Can you send a proposal that shows options for (a) an increased commit with stepped true-ups, and (b) a mixed model where we keep a smaller committed baseline + priced burst capacity?

Key constraints: finance needs a maximum effective per-token rate for FY27 into the PO (price hold window to cover Jan–Mar 2027 ramp). Also prefer a one-page Mutual Action Plan with milestones.

-Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Product Ops, Atlas Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation kickoff — capacity growth ask

Maya —

Appreciate the clarity. Attaching a first-pass proposal (Atlas_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf) and an Excel with three commit scenarios (Commit_Tier_Scenarios.xlsx). High-level thoughts:

- Heterogeneous commit (our term): combine a modest baseline commit that covers core production tokens + a priced burst pool with a guaranteed unit price ceiling (price-hold) for Q1 to protect you while traffic ramps.
- Scenario A (Conservative): 1.5x baseline commit; 10% volume discount; no burst guarantee.
- Scenario B (Hybrid): 1.0x baseline commit + burst pool sized for 1.5x peak; 12% blended discount; explicit price-hold for Jan–Mar 2027 with a cap on effective per-token.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): 2.5x baseline commit; 18% discount band; smaller burst. This reduces unit cost but requires greater up-front commit.

We also propose a credit buffer that can be used for overage in the first 90 days post-go-live to smooth any measurement/ingestion variances. If they prefer, we can convert that buffer into invoice credits applied retroactively once usage normalizes.

Next steps from our side: finance will model ARR impact and I’ll sync with Laura on SLA and legal on a limited price-hold clause. Can you confirm which scenario you want to review with procurement?

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Atlas_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf)

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation kickoff — capacity growth ask

Karthik / Maya —

Procurement flagged two asks: (1) we need an explicit PO-ready price-hold clause for Jan–Mar 2027 (language that binds the effective per-token ceiling for that period), and (2) we need a clear true-up cadence (quarterly vs monthly) with thresholds for automatic credit application.

Also, finance prefers invoice credits rather than up-front prepayments.

If you can provide proposed contract text and a one-page MAP, procurement can turn this into a PO the week of Dec 6.

Thanks,
John
Director, Vendor Management — Atlas Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: proposed price-hold language + credit mechanics

Team —

Draft language below for procurement’s ask; please sanity-check and we’ll pass to legal.

1) Price-hold clause (Jan 1–Mar 31, 2027): Redwood will guarantee that the effective per-token rate charged for Atlas Health’s production usage will not exceed $0.00185 per token (blended across generation and embedding units) for the stated period. Any usage billed above the committed baseline but within the documented burst pool will be billed at or below this ceiling.

2) True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups with an automatic credit applied if measured usage falls below the committed baseline during a quarter (credit applied to the following invoice). Monthly usage reporting will be provided within 10 business days of month-end.

3) Credit buffer mechanics: Redwood will provide a one-time 10% credit of the committed baseline to be used within the first 90 days post-start date; unused portion converts to a credit on the subsequent invoice.

Ben — can you run revenue impact scenarios for Hybrid (Scenario B) and Aggressive (Scenario C)? Monica — please draft a 1-page MAP with milestones: signature, go-live, 30/60/90 check-ins, and PO issuance.

-Laura
VP, Commercial Ops
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: proposed price-hold language + credit mechanics

Ack — I ran the numbers. Scenario B (Hybrid) yields a ~12.4% blended ASP reduction and keeps ARR accretion within our target band; converting the credit buffer to invoice credit (vs prepayment) is neutral to cash in the first quarter, negative to cashflow but preferred by Atlas. Recommend we accept invoice-credit mechanics.

I'll attach a short summary table for legal/finance to review in the morning.

Ben
Head of Revenue Ops
(attachment: Commit_Tier_Scenarios.xlsx)
